value.requirements/s3_zip_manifest/assumptions:
# s3_zip_manifest: assumptions and decisions

## Answers

- SUG-5 (suggestion): The bucket is versioned. If the same key is uploaded again between SEP-1 and SEP-2, a plain DeleteObject puts a delete marker on top of the NEW version, so a fresh upload disappears until someone notices. The second event then finds the source gone and is skipped. → accepted: SEP-1 stores the source VersionId from HeadObject in vars.source_version_id. SEP-2 becomes custom code: head the source and delete only when the current VersionId equals vars.source_version_id (DeleteObject with that VersionId). Otherwise it leaves the object alone and logs a WARNING (the new upload has its own event). The uses: s3.delete entry would be dropped.
- SUG-6 (suggestion): staging_prefix stays 'staging_test/' in every environment (Q-ENV-1 got no answer, so the owner's value is kept). → accepted: Set staging_prefix to 'staging/' in dev, test and prod, and update the lifecycle rule to match.
- SUG-7 (suggestion): The S3 notification is shared with an existing QueueConfiguration whose filter is unknown. A wrong overlap makes PutBucketNotificationConfiguration fail. → accepted: The IaC deployment fails with a clear message when an existing rule overlaps prefix {incoming_prefix} / suffix .zip, so the owner can apply the Q-TRG-1 decision before anything is changed.

## Assumptions

- Q-TRG-1 accepted: IaC adds one QueueConfiguration (ObjectCreated:*, prefix {incoming_prefix}, suffix .zip) to the new queue and keeps the existing rules; on overlap the owner decides.
- Q-SEP-1-1 accepted, combined with SUG-2: dedupe uses the index object {index_prefix}{stem}/{source_sha256}_{source_key_hash}.json written by DLP-1 instead of listing outgoing/. SEP-1 also verifies that the referenced outgoing object still has a matching pkf-source-sha256 before it deletes the original.
- SUG-1 accepted: lifecycle rule for noncurrent versions (30 days) under incoming, processing and staging, plus expired delete marker removal.
- SUG-3 accepted: report written to s3://{target_bucket}/{report_prefix}{run_id}.json; report_prefix dev value reports/s3_zip_manifest/.
- SUG-4 accepted: max_packages = 100.
- index_prefix dev value 'index/s3_zip_manifest/' is derived (owner named the setting only).
- Unanswered non-blocking proposals adopted: Q-SEP-2-1 (s3.delete with defaults, missing_ok), Q-TRN-1-1 (group TRN-1+TRN-2), Q-TRN-1-2 (manifest format; root manifest.csv → DataError), Q-SRC-1 (sub-folders accepted, names by stem; collisions → DataError), Q-SRC-2 (current version, WARNING on size mismatch), Q-SEP-1-2 (replay skip/resume), Q-TRG-2 (DLQ, maxReceiveCount 3, visibility 21600 s, SSE-SQS, queue policy), Q-NF-1 (≥ 8 GiB scratch, 3×size+10% check → TransientError), Q-DLP-1-1 (skip_identical; different sha → DataError).
- Q-ENV-1 got no answer: the owner's staging_prefix 'staging_test/' is kept (see SUG-6).
- Encryption: no sse param; objects inherit the bucket default SSE-KMS key; IAM grants kms:Decrypt/GenerateDataKey on it.
- No loop: the pipeline writes only to processing, staging, outgoing, index and reports, never under incoming/.
- Examples 2–4 are derived; example 1 is quoted from SEP-1/TRN-1 (zip contents derived).

## Derived examples

- replayed_message_source_gone
- zip_with_root_manifest_fails
- outgoing_collision_not_overwritten
value.requirements/s3_zip_manifest/contracts.y:
- after: SEP-0
  fields:
  - name: package_id
    type: str
    meaning: stable id (message id)
  - name: name
    type: str
    meaning: base file name, e.g. study_a.zip
  - name: source.bucket
    type: str
    meaning: event bucket
  - name: source.key
    type: str
    meaning: exact event key under incoming/
  - name: source.size
    type: int
    meaning: size from the event
  - name: source.event_time
    type: str
    meaning: ISO-8601 UTC event time
  - name: source.message_id
    type: str
    meaning: SQS message id
  - name: source.receipt_handle
    type: str
    meaning: SQS receipt handle
  - name: vars.package_ts
    type: str
    meaning: event time as YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ
  - name: vars.stem
    type: str
    meaning: name without .zip
  - name: vars.ext
    type: str
    meaning: .zip
  s3_objects:
  - bucket: source_bucket
    key: '{incoming_prefix}{name}'
    meaning: original package (absent for a replay)
- after: SEP-1
  fields:
  - name: status
    type: str
    meaning: ok, or skipped (already delivered / replay)
  - name: vars.source_sha256
    type: str
    meaning: sha256 of the original zip
  - name: vars.source_key
    type: str
    meaning: original source key
  - name: vars.source_key_hash
    type: str
    meaning: sha1(source_key)[:12]
  - name: artefacts.renamed_key
    type: str
    meaning: '{processing_prefix}{stem}_{package_ts}.zip'
  s3_objects:
  - bucket: source_bucket
    key: '{processing_prefix}{stem}_{package_ts}.zip'
    meaning: verified copy of the original
  - bucket: source_bucket
    key: '{incoming_prefix}{name}'
    meaning: original still present
- after: SEP-2
  fields:
  - name: artefacts.renamed_key
    type: str
    meaning: processing copy key
  - name: vars.source_sha256
    type: str
    meaning: source sha
  s3_objects:
  - bucket: source_bucket
    key: '{processing_prefix}{stem}_{package_ts}.zip'
    meaning: only copy of the package; incoming original deleted
- after: TRN-1
  fields:
  - name: artefacts.new_zip_path
    type: str
    meaning: local path in rt.shared_dir() of the rebuilt zip (valid only inside the TRN group); absent when vars.staged
  - name: vars.staged
    type: bool
    meaning: true when the staging zip already existed
  - name: vars.manifest_rows
    type: int
    meaning: number of manifest rows (when built)
  s3_objects:
  - bucket: source_bucket
    key: '{processing_prefix}{stem}_{package_ts}.zip'
    meaning: processing copy
- after: TRN-2
  fields:
  - name: artefacts.staging_key
    type: str
    meaning: '{staging_prefix}{stem}_{package_ts}.zip'
  s3_objects:
  - bucket: target_bucket
    key: '{staging_prefix}{stem}_{package_ts}.zip'
    meaning: rebuilt zip with manifest.csv, metadata pkf-source-key/pkf-source-sha256/pkf-sha256
- after: DLP-1
  fields:
  - name: artefacts.outgoing_key
    type: str
    meaning: '{outgoing_prefix}{package_ts}_{stem}.zip'
  - name: artefacts.index_key
    type: str
    meaning: delivery index key
  s3_objects:
  - bucket: target_bucket
    key: '{outgoing_prefix}{package_ts}_{stem}.zip'
    meaning: delivered package
  - bucket: target_bucket
    key: '{index_prefix}{stem}/{source_sha256}_{source_key_hash}.json'
    meaning: delivery index
- after: DLP-2
  fields:
  - name: artefacts.outgoing_key
    type: str
    meaning: delivered key
  s3_objects:
  - bucket: target_bucket
    key: '{outgoing_prefix}{package_ts}_{stem}.zip'
    meaning: delivered package; processing and staging copies deleted

- name: happy_path_study_a
  origin: quoted
  given:
  - bucket: source_bucket
    key: incoming/study_a.zip
    zip:
      a.pdf: 0123456789
      b/c.pdf: 01234567890123456789
  then_present:
  - bucket: target_bucket
    key: ^outgoing/20261022T100000Z_study_a\.zip$
    zip_entries:
    - a.pdf
    - b/c.pdf
    - manifest.csv
  - bucket: target_bucket
    key: ^index/s3_zip_manifest/study_a/[0-9a-f]{64}_[0-9a-f]{12}\.json$
  then_absent:
  - bucket: source_bucket
    key: incoming/study_a.zip
  - bucket: source_bucket
    key: processing/study_a_20261022T100000Z.zip
  - bucket: target_bucket
    key: staging_test/study_a_20261022T100000Z.zip
  fail_packages: 0
- name: replayed_message_source_gone
  origin: derived
  given: []
  events:
  - bucket: source_bucket
    key: incoming/study_b.zip
  then_present: []
  then_absent:
  - bucket: target_bucket
    key: outgoing/20261022T100000Z_study_b.zip
  - bucket: source_bucket
    key: processing/study_b_20261022T100000Z.zip
  fail_packages: 0
- name: zip_with_root_manifest_fails
  origin: derived
  given:
  - bucket: source_bucket
    key: incoming/study_c.zip
    zip:
      a.pdf: x
      manifest.csv: old
  then_present:
  - bucket: source_bucket
    key: ^processing/study_c_20261022T100000Z\.zip$
    zip_entries:
    - a.pdf
    - manifest.csv
  then_absent:
  - bucket: source_bucket
    key: incoming/study_c.zip
  - bucket: target_bucket
    key: outgoing/20261022T100000Z_study_c.zip
  fail_packages: 1
- name: outgoing_collision_not_overwritten
  origin: derived
  given:
  - bucket: target_bucket
    key: outgoing/20261022T100000Z_study_d.zip
    content: other
  - bucket: source_bucket
    key: incoming/study_d.zip
    zip:
      a.pdf: x
  then_present:
  - bucket: target_bucket
    key: ^outgoing/20261022T100000Z_study_d\.zip$
  - bucket: target_bucket
    key: ^staging_test/study_d_20261022T100000Z\.zip$
    zip_entries:
    - a.pdf
    - manifest.csv
  - bucket: source_bucket
    key: ^processing/study_d_20261022T100000Z\.zip$
  then_absent:
  - bucket: source_bucket
    key: incoming/study_d.zip
  fail_packages: 1

  - name: aws_account

    values:
      dev: dev-dpl-dstore-sas-eu-north-1-992382551516

    description: delivery bucket; the same bucket as the source
    secret_ref: false
  - name: incoming_prefix
    values:
      dev: incoming/

      prod: incoming/
    description: watched prefix (S3 notification filter, suffix .zip)
    secret_ref: false

      test: processing/
      prod: processing/
    description: renamed working copy of the original zip
    secret_ref: false

      dev: staging_test/
      test: staging_test/
      prod: staging_test/
    description: rebuilt zip with manifest.csv before delivery (owner's value kept, see SUG-6)
    secret_ref: false

      dev: outgoing/
      test: outgoing/
      prod: outgoing/

    secret_ref: false

  - name: report_prefix
    values:
      dev: reports/s3_zip_manifest/
    description: run reports s3://{target_bucket}/{report_prefix}{run_id}.json (SUG-3); value derived from the owner's example
    secret_ref: false
  - name: queue_url
    values:
      dev: create
      test: create
      prod: create
    description: SQS queue receiving S3 ObjectCreated events for {incoming_prefix}*.zip
    secret_ref: false
  - name: dlq_url
    values:
      dev: create
    description: dead-letter queue of queue_url, maxReceiveCount 3 (Q-TRG-2 proposal)
    secret_ref: false
  - name: kms_key_arn
    values:
      dev: arn:aws:kms:eu-north-1:992382551516:key/65f013e6-0620-4f49-a814-ce30d321f3dc
    description: the bucket's default SSE-KMS key, used for IAM only; derived from the probe
    secret_ref: false
  - name: aws_conn_id
    values:
      dev: aws_default
      test: aws_default
      prod: aws_default
    description: Airflow connection (no secrets)
    secret_ref: false
  - name: alert_email
    values:
      dev: ''
    description: data-engineering team e-mail address for alerts
    secret_ref: false
  overview: 'A user or a source process uploads a zip package of PDFs under incoming/. S3 sends an event notification to an
    SQS

    queue; an hourly DAG reads the messages, adds a manifest.csv to every package and delivers it under outgoing/.'
  source: S3 bucket {source_bucket}, prefix {incoming_prefix}. Packages are zip files of PDFs, up to 2 GB.
  destination: S3 bucket {target_bucket}, prefix {outgoing_prefix}. An existing object is never overwritten.
  nonfunctional: 'Up to 50 packages an hour, largest zip 2 GB. Retries: 2. Alerts by e-mail to the data engineering team.

    Data classification: internal; objects use the bucket''s default encryption.'
  trigger:
    kind: sqs
    schedule: 0 * * * *
    queue: queue_url
    bucket: source_bucket
    prefix: incoming_prefix
    suffix: .zip
    timezone: UTC
    text: 'sqs: { queue: queue_url, poll: "0 * * * *" }

      S3 ObjectCreated events for incoming/*.zip go to the queue; the DAG polls it every hour (UTC), one active run.'
  units:
  - id: SEP-1
    lane: sep
    number: 1
    title: Copy and rename the package
    does: 'Check whether the package''s source object (ctx.source.key) exists. If it does: compute its sha256 and look for
      the delivery index object {index_prefix}{stem}/{source_sha256}_{source_key_hash}.json. When the index exists, its source_key
      equals the source key, and the referenced outgoing object still exists with metadata pkf-source-sha256 equal to the
      sha: delete the incoming original and mark the package skipped. Otherwise server-side copy the source to {processing_prefix}{stem}_{package_ts}.zip
      in {source_bucket}, verified by size and sha256 (skip_identical). If the source is gone: resume from an existing processing
      copy, else skip with a WARNING (replay).'
    level: package
    on_failure: fail_package
    uses: null
    params: {}
    example: null
    line: 0
  - id: SEP-2
    lane: sep
    number: 2
    title: Remove the original
    does: Delete the package's own source object (ctx.source.bucket/ctx.source.key, the exact key from the event). An object
      that is already gone is fine. It runs only when SEP-1 left status ok, which means the processing copy is verified (skipped
      packages pass through).
    level: package
    on_failure: fail_package
    uses: s3.delete
    params:
      missing_ok: true
    example: null
    line: 0
  - id: TRN-1
    lane: trn
    number: 1
    title: Build the manifest
    does: 'Unless a staging zip for this package already exists with matching pkf-source-sha256: check free disk space, then
      download artefacts.renamed_key to rt.shared_dir() and safe-extract it. Build manifest.csv with columns file_name,size_bytes
      (header row; one row per non-folder entry in zip order; file_name is the path inside the zip, size_bytes the uncompressed
      size). Build a new zip64 with the original files plus manifest.csv at the root. Hand over its path in artefacts.new_zip_path.'
    level: package
    on_failure: fail_package
    uses: null
    params: {}
    example: null
    line: 0
  - id: TRN-2
    lane: trn
    number: 2
    title: Upload to staging
    does: Upload artefacts.new_zip_path to {staging_prefix}{stem}_{package_ts}.zip in {target_bucket}, with metadata pkf-source-key=vars.source_key
      and pkf-source-sha256=vars.source_sha256 (pkf-sha256 is added by the kit), if_exists=fail. Hand over the key as artefacts.staging_key.
      When TRN-1 found the staging zip already done (vars.staged), do nothing.
    level: package
    on_failure: fail_package
    uses: null
    params: {}
    example: null
    line: 0
  - id: DLP-1
    lane: dlp
    number: 1
    title: Deliver to outgoing
    does: Verified server-side copy of artefacts.staging_key to {outgoing_prefix}{package_ts}_{stem}.zip in {target_bucket}
      with if_exists=skip_identical (never overwrite; a different existing object raises DataError). Then check that the outgoing
      object carries pkf-source-key and pkf-source-sha256 equal to the vars. Finally write the delivery index object {index_prefix}{stem}/{source_sha256}_{source_key_hash}.json.
    level: package
    on_failure: fail_package
    uses: null
    params: {}
    example: null
    line: 0
  - id: DLP-2
    lane: dlp
    number: 2
    title: Clean up
    does: After confirming that artefacts.outgoing_key exists in {target_bucket}, delete artefacts.renamed_key (processing
      copy, source_bucket) and artefacts.staging_key (target_bucket), missing_ok. A failure here does not fail the package.
    level: package
    on_failure: skip
    uses: null
    params: {}
    example: null
    line: 0
  transformation_none: false
  dag:
    order:
    - SEP-1
    - SEP-2
    - TRN-1
    - TRN-2
    - DLP-1
    - DLP-2
    text: SEP-1 → SEP-2 → TRN-1 → TRN-2 → DLP-1 → DLP-2
    generated: false
units:
  SEP-1:
    id: SEP-1
    title: Copy and rename the package

      the delivery index object {index_prefix}{stem}/{source_sha256}_{source_key_hash}.json. When the index exists, its source_key
      equals the source key, and the referenced outgoing object still exists with metadata pkf-source-sha256 equal to the
      sha: delete the incoming original and mark the package skipped. Otherwise server-side copy the source to {processing_prefix}{stem}_{package_ts}.zip
      in {source_bucket}, verified by size and sha256 (skip_identical). If the source is gone: resume from an existing processing
      copy, else skip with a WARNING (replay).'
    level: package
    on_failure: fail_package
    uses: ''
    settings_used:

    - target_bucket
    - processing_prefix
    - outgoing_prefix
    - index_prefix

    - target_bucket:{index_prefix}{stem}/{source_sha256}_{source_key_hash}.json
    - target_bucket:{outgoing_prefix}*_{stem}.zip (head only, the key from the index)
    - source_bucket:{processing_prefix}{stem}_{package_ts}.zip
    writes:
    - source_bucket:{processing_prefix}{stem}_{package_ts}.zip
    - delete source_bucket:{source.key} (only on a verified earlier delivery)
    idempotency: 'verified_copy with if_exists=skip_identical: a target with the same sha counts as done, a different sha
      raises DataError. When the source is already gone, the existing processing copy is resumed; with no processing copy
      either, the package is skipped.'
    side_effects:
    - may delete the incoming original when the index proves an earlier verified delivery
    edge_cases: []
    clauses:
    - id: R-SEP-1-a
      text: The processing key is {processing_prefix}{stem}_{package_ts}.zip, where package_ts is the S3 event time in YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ
        UTC.
    - id: R-SEP-1-b
      text: The copy is verified by size and sha256, never by ETag. A different existing target raises DataError.
    - id: R-SEP-1-c
      text: A package counts as already delivered only when the index object for (stem, source sha256, source key hash) exists,
        its source_key equals ctx.source.key, and its outgoing object exists with pkf-source-sha256 == source sha256. Then
        the original is deleted and status=skipped.
    - id: R-SEP-1-d
      text: Source gone + processing copy present → resume. Source gone + no processing copy → status skipped with a WARNING
        (message is deleted by ack).
    - id: R-SEP-1-e
      text: When the current source size differs from ctx.source.size, log a WARNING and process the current version.
    helpers:
    - name: source_key_hash
      signature: 'def source_key_hash(key: str) -> str'
      purpose: stable short hash of the source key for the index name
      pseudocode: return hashlib.sha1(key.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()[:12]
    - name: index_key
      signature: 'def index_key(rt: Runtime, stem: str, sha: str, key_hash: str) -> str'
      purpose: render the delivery index key
      pseudocode: return check_key(render('{index_prefix}{stem}/{sha}_{h}.json', index_prefix=rt.settings['index_prefix'],
        stem=stem, sha=sha, h=key_hash))
    pseudocode: "1. s3 = rt.s3(); src_b = ctx.source.bucket; src_k = ctx.source.key; stem = ctx.vars['stem']; ts = ctx.vars['package_ts'].\n\
      2. proc_key = check_key(f\"{rt.settings['processing_prefix']}{stem}_{ts}.zip\"); kh = source_key_hash(src_k).\n3. h\
      \ = head(s3, src_b, src_k).\n4. If h is None:\n   a. ph = head(s3, rt.settings['source_bucket'], proc_key). If ph: sha\
      \ = sha256_of(s3, source_bucket, proc_key); set vars source_sha256=sha, source_key_hash=kh, source_key=src_k; artefacts.renamed_key=proc_key;\
      \ log INFO 'resume'; return ctx.\n   b. Else log WARNING 'source gone, nothing to resume'; ctx.status='skipped'; return\
      \ ctx.\n5. If ctx.source.size is not None and h['size'] != ctx.source.size: log WARNING.\n6. sha = sha256_of(s3, src_b,\
      \ src_k).\n7. ik = index_key(rt, stem, sha, kh); obj = head(s3, target_bucket, ik).\n8. If obj: download it to rt.tmpdir()\
      \ and json-load it → idx. If idx['source_key'] == src_k: oh = head(s3, target_bucket, idx['outgoing_key']). If oh and\
      \ oh.metadata['pkf-source-sha256'] == sha: delete(s3, src_b, src_k, missing_ok=True); ctx.status='skipped'; vars.already_delivered=idx['outgoing_key'];\
      \ return ctx.\n9. verified_copy(s3, src_b, src_k, rt.settings['source_bucket'], proc_key, if_exists='skip_identical')\
      \ (a different existing sha → DataError).\n10. Set vars source_sha256=sha, source_key_hash=kh, source_key=src_k; artefacts.renamed_key=proc_key;\
      \ return ctx."
    aws_calls:
    - s3:HeadObject {source_bucket}/{incoming_prefix}*
    - s3:GetObject {source_bucket}/{incoming_prefix}*
    - s3:HeadObject {target_bucket}/{index_prefix}*
    - s3:GetObject {target_bucket}/{index_prefix}*
    - s3:HeadObject {target_bucket}/{outgoing_prefix}*
    - s3:CopyObject {source_bucket}/{incoming_prefix}* -> {source_bucket}/{processing_prefix}*
    - s3:HeadObject {source_bucket}/{processing_prefix}*
    - s3:DeleteObject {source_bucket}/{incoming_prefix}*
    params: {}
  SEP-2:
    id: SEP-2
    title: Remove the original
    does: Delete the package's own source object (ctx.source.bucket/ctx.source.key, the exact key from the event). An object
      that is already gone is fine. It runs only when SEP-1 left status ok, which means the processing copy is verified (skipped
      packages pass through).
    level: package
    on_failure: fail_package
    uses: s3.delete
    settings_used: []
    reads: []
    writes:
    - delete source_bucket:{source.key}
    idempotency: 'missing_ok=true: a second run finds the object gone and does nothing.'
    side_effects:
    - adds a delete marker (versioned bucket); the noncurrent version expires after 30 days via the lifecycle rule
    edge_cases: []
    clauses:
    - id: R-SEP-2-a
      text: Delete the source only after SEP-1 verified the processing copy (guaranteed by the order and status ok).
    - id: R-SEP-2-b
      text: bucket/key default to ctx.source; the owner's '{incoming_prefix}{name}.zip' template is replaced because {name}
        already holds '.zip'.
    helpers: []
    pseudocode: '1. run_op(''s3.delete'', ctx, rt, {''missing_ok'': True}): delete ctx.source.bucket/ctx.source.key.

      2. Return ctx.'
    aws_calls:
    - s3:DeleteObject {source_bucket}/{incoming_prefix}*
    params:
      missing_ok: true
  TRN-1:
    id: TRN-1
    title: Build the manifest

# s3_zip_manifest: pseudocode

## Source extraction pattern

### SEP-1: Copy and rename the package

Check whether the package's source object (ctx.source.key) exists. If it does: compute its sha256 and look for the delivery index object {index_prefix}{stem}/{source_sha256}_{source_key_hash}.json. When the index exists, its source_key equals the source key, and the referenced outgoing object still exists with metadata pkf-source-sha256 equal to the sha: delete the incoming original and mark the package skipped. Otherwise server-side copy the source to {processing_prefix}{stem}_{package_ts}.zip in {source_bucket}, verified by size and sha256 (skip_identical). If the source is gone: resume from an existing processing copy, else skip with a WARNING (replay).

*Level:* package · *on failure:* fail_package · *idempotency:* verified_copy with if_exists=skip_identical: a target with the same sha counts as done, a different sha raises DataError. When the source is already gone, the existing processing copy is resumed; with no processing copy either, the package is skipped.

```text
1. s3 = rt.s3(); src_b = ctx.source.bucket; src_k = ctx.source.key; stem = ctx.vars['stem']; ts = ctx.vars['package_ts'].
2. proc_key = check_key(f"{rt.settings['processing_prefix']}{stem}_{ts}.zip"); kh = source_key_hash(src_k).
3. h = head(s3, src_b, src_k).
4. If h is None:
   a. ph = head(s3, rt.settings['source_bucket'], proc_key). If ph: sha = sha256_of(s3, source_bucket, proc_key); set vars source_sha256=sha, source_key_hash=kh, source_key=src_k; artefacts.renamed_key=proc_key; log INFO 'resume'; return ctx.
   b. Else log WARNING 'source gone, nothing to resume'; ctx.status='skipped'; return ctx.
5. If ctx.source.size is not None and h['size'] != ctx.source.size: log WARNING.
6. sha = sha256_of(s3, src_b, src_k).
7. ik = index_key(rt, stem, sha, kh); obj = head(s3, target_bucket, ik).
8. If obj: download it to rt.tmpdir() and json-load it → idx. If idx['source_key'] == src_k: oh = head(s3, target_bucket, idx['outgoing_key']). If oh and oh.metadata['pkf-source-sha256'] == sha: delete(s3, src_b, src_k, missing_ok=True); ctx.status='skipped'; vars.already_delivered=idx['outgoing_key']; return ctx.
9. verified_copy(s3, src_b, src_k, rt.settings['source_bucket'], proc_key, if_exists='skip_identical') (a different existing sha → DataError).
10. Set vars source_sha256=sha, source_key_hash=kh, source_key=src_k; artefacts.renamed_key=proc_key; return ctx.
```

- helper `def source_key_hash(key: str) -> str`: stable short hash of the source key for the index name

  ```text
  return hashlib.sha1(key.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()[:12]
  ```
- helper `def index_key(rt: Runtime, stem: str, sha: str, key_hash: str) -> str`: render the delivery index key

  ```text
  return check_key(render('{index_prefix}{stem}/{sha}_{h}.json', index_prefix=rt.settings['index_prefix'], stem=stem, sha=sha, h=key_hash))
  ```
- clauses: R-SEP-1-a The processing key is {processing_prefix}{stem}_{package_ts}.zip, where package_ts is the S3 event time in YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ UTC., R-SEP-1-b The copy is verified by size and sha256, never by ETag. A different existing target raises DataError., R-SEP-1-c A package counts as already delivered only when the index object for (stem, source sha256, source key hash) exists, its source_key equals ctx.source.key, and its outgoing object exists with pkf-source-sha256 == source sha256. Then the original is deleted and status=skipped., R-SEP-1-d Source gone + processing copy present → resume. Source gone + no processing copy → status skipped with a WARNING (message is deleted by ack)., R-SEP-1-e When the current source size differs from ctx.source.size, log a WARNING and process the current version.
- edge cases: —

### SEP-2: Remove the original

Delete the package's own source object (ctx.source.bucket/ctx.source.key, the exact key from the event). An object that is already gone is fine. It runs only when SEP-1 left status ok, which means the processing copy is verified (skipped packages pass through).

*Level:* package · *on failure:* fail_package · *idempotency:* missing_ok=true: a second run finds the object gone and does nothing.

Kit operation `s3.delete` with `{"missing_ok": true}`.

- clauses: R-SEP-2-a Delete the source only after SEP-1 verified the processing copy (guaranteed by the order and status ok)., R-SEP-2-b bucket/key default to ctx.source; the owner's '{incoming_prefix}{name}.zip' template is replaced because {name} already holds '.zip'.
- edge cases: —

## Transformation

### TRN-1: Build the manifest

Unless a staging zip for this package already exists with matching pkf-source-sha256: check free disk space, then download artefacts.renamed_key to rt.shared_dir() and safe-extract it. Build manifest.csv with columns file_name,size_bytes (header row; one row per non-folder entry in zip order; file_name is the path inside the zip, size_bytes the uncompressed size). Build a new zip64 with the original files plus manifest.csv at the root. Hand over its path in artefacts.new_zip_path.

*Level:* package · *on failure:* fail_package · *idempotency:* When the staging zip already exists with pkf-source-sha256 == vars.source_sha256, it sets artefacts.staging_key and builds nothing; a staging zip with a different source sha raises DataError. Otherwise it is a pure local rebuild in shared_dir.

```text
1. s3=rt.s3(); stem, ts = vars; stg_key = check_key(f"{rt.settings['staging_prefix']}{stem}_{ts}.zip").
2. sh = head(s3, target_bucket, stg_key). If sh: if sh.metadata.get('pkf-source-sha256') == vars.source_sha256: artefacts.staging_key=stg_key; vars.staged=True; return ctx. Else raise DataError('staging object exists for another source').
3. d = rt.shared_dir(); ph = head(s3, source_bucket, artefacts.renamed_key); ensure_disk(d, ph['size']).
4. zp = download(s3, source_bucket, artefacts.renamed_key, d/'in.zip').
5. ents = entries(zp); if any(e['name']=='manifest.csv' for e in ents): raise DataError.
6. files = safe_extract(zp, d/'x'); map each entry name to d/'x'/name.
7. m = build_manifest(ents, d/'manifest.csv').
8. out = make_zip([(d/'x'/e['name'], e['name']) for e in ents if not e['is_dir']] + [(m,'manifest.csv')], d/'out.zip').
9. Delete in.zip to free space; artefacts.new_zip_path=str(out); vars.manifest_rows=len(non-folder entries); return ctx.
```

- helper `def build_manifest(entries: list[dict], dest: Path) -> Path`: write manifest.csv from zip entries

  ```text
  rows=[(e['name'], e['size']) for e in entries if not e['is_dir']]; open dest 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline=''; csv.writer(f, lineterminator='\n', quoting=csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL); writerow(['file_name','size_bytes']); writerows(rows); return dest
  ```
- helper `def ensure_disk(path: Path, zip_size: int) -> None`: guard the worker disk

  ```text
  free=shutil.disk_usage(path).free; if free < int(zip_size*3*1.1): raise TransientError(f'need {..} bytes, free {free}')
  ```
- clauses: R-TRN-1-a manifest.csv: UTF-8 without BOM, comma separator, RFC 4180 quoting, LF line endings, header file_name,size_bytes, rows in zip entry order, every non-folder entry (not only .pdf)., R-TRN-1-b A zip that already contains a root manifest.csv fails the package with DataError., R-TRN-1-c Extraction uses archive.safe_extract (zip-slip, symlinks and bombs → DataError)., R-TRN-1-d Before downloading, free space in shared_dir must be ≥ 3 × zip size × 1.1, else TransientError., R-TRN-1-e TRN-1 and TRN-2 share one Airflow task (group); the local zip path is handed over in artefacts.new_zip_path.
- edge cases: —

### TRN-2: Upload to staging

Upload artefacts.new_zip_path to {staging_prefix}{stem}_{package_ts}.zip in {target_bucket}, with metadata pkf-source-key=vars.source_key and pkf-source-sha256=vars.source_sha256 (pkf-sha256 is added by the kit), if_exists=fail. Hand over the key as artefacts.staging_key. When TRN-1 found the staging zip already done (vars.staged), do nothing.

*Level:* package · *on failure:* fail_package · *idempotency:* TRN-1 detects an existing staging zip for the same source sha and sets vars.staged, so the upload is skipped. Written under the final name only.

```text
1. If vars.get('staged'): return ctx (staging_key already set).
2. key = check_key(f"{rt.settings['staging_prefix']}{vars.stem}_{vars.package_ts}.zip").
3. upload(rt.s3(), Path(artefacts.new_zip_path), target_bucket, key, if_exists='fail', metadata={'pkf-source-key': vars.source_key, 'pkf-source-sha256': vars.source_sha256}).
4. artefacts.staging_key = key; return ctx.
```

- clauses: R-TRN-2-a The staging zip carries user metadata pkf-source-key and pkf-source-sha256., R-TRN-2-b artefacts.staging_key is set in every ok path.
- edge cases: —

## Destination load pattern

### DLP-1: Deliver to outgoing

Verified server-side copy of artefacts.staging_key to {outgoing_prefix}{package_ts}_{stem}.zip in {target_bucket} with if_exists=skip_identical (never overwrite; a different existing object raises DataError). Then check that the outgoing object carries pkf-source-key and pkf-source-sha256 equal to the vars. Finally write the delivery index object {index_prefix}{stem}/{source_sha256}_{source_key_hash}.json.

*Level:* package · *on failure:* fail_package · *idempotency:* skip_identical on both writes. The index content is deterministic (sorted keys, no run clock), so a re-run finds identical objects.

```text
1. s3=rt.s3(); tb=rt.settings['target_bucket']; out_key=check_key(f"{outgoing_prefix}{package_ts}_{stem}.zip").
2. r = verified_copy(s3, tb, artefacts.staging_key, tb, out_key, if_exists='skip_identical').
3. oh = head(s3, tb, out_key); if oh.metadata.get('pkf-source-key')!=vars.source_key or oh.metadata.get('pkf-source-sha256')!=vars.source_sha256: raise DataError.
4. idx = {source_key, source_sha256, outgoing_key: out_key, outgoing_sha256: sha256_of(s3,tb,out_key), package_ts}; write json.dumps(idx, sort_keys=True) to rt.tmpdir()/'idx.json'.
5. ik = index_key(rt, stem, source_sha256, source_key_hash); upload(s3, path, tb, ik, if_exists='skip_identical').
6. artefacts.outgoing_key=out_key; artefacts.index_key=ik; return ctx.
```

- clauses: R-DLP-1-a Outgoing name {outgoing_prefix}{package_ts}_{stem}.zip; an existing object is never overwritten., R-DLP-1-b After the copy, the outgoing metadata pkf-source-key/pkf-source-sha256 must equal vars.source_key/vars.source_sha256, else DataError., R-DLP-1-c Index JSON = {"source_key", "source_sha256", "outgoing_key", "outgoing_sha256", "package_ts"}, sort_keys, written only after the outgoing object is verified.
- edge cases: —

### DLP-2: Clean up

After confirming that artefacts.outgoing_key exists in {target_bucket}, delete artefacts.renamed_key (processing copy, source_bucket) and artefacts.staging_key (target_bucket), missing_ok. A failure here does not fail the package.

*Level:* package · *on failure:* skip · *idempotency:* Deletes with missing_ok=True.

```text
1. If head(s3, target_bucket, artefacts.outgoing_key) is None: log WARNING; return ctx.
2. delete(s3, source_bucket, artefacts.renamed_key, missing_ok=True).
3. delete(s3, target_bucket, artefacts.staging_key, missing_ok=True).
4. Return ctx.
```

- clauses: R-DLP-2-a Delete only when head(outgoing_key) succeeds; otherwise log a WARNING and keep both copies.
- edge cases: —

## DAG

DAG s3_zip_manifest: schedule '0 * * * *' UTC, catchup=False, max_active_runs=1, dagrun_timeout 5 h (below the 6 h SQS visibility timeout).
start → SEP-0 discover (sqs, queue_url, max_packages 100; drops TestEvents and duplicates) → per package (dynamic task mapping, max 8 parallel): SEP-1 (timeout 60 min) → SEP-2 (10 min) → [TRN-1 + TRN-2 in one Airflow task, shared_dir, timeout 120 min, worker scratch ≥ 8 GiB] → DLP-1 (60 min) → DLP-2 (10 min, on_failure skip) → outcome → DLP-Z ack (delete delivered/skipped handles, release failed) → report (write_uri s3://{target_bucket}/{report_prefix}{run_id}.json; RunFailed when any failed) → end.
Retries: 2 per task, retry_delay 5 min, exponential backoff, only for TransientError and unexpected errors. DataError fails the package without a retry; ConfigError fails the run. E-mail on task failure and on RunFailed to alert_email.

Order: start → SEP-0 discover → package[ SEP-1 → SEP-2 → TRN-1 → TRN-2 → DLP-1 → DLP-2 → outcome ] → DLP-Z ack → report → end

- name: incoming prefix
  kind: s3_prefix
  setting: incoming_prefix
  status: existing
  actions:
  - s3:GetObject
  - s3:DeleteObject
  details: watched prefix; the pipeline never writes here (no loop)
- name: processing prefix
  kind: s3_prefix
  setting: processing_prefix
  status: create
  actions:
  - s3:GetObject
  - s3:PutObject
  - s3:DeleteObject
  details: SEP-1 writes, TRN-1 reads, DLP-2 deletes
- name: staging prefix
  kind: s3_prefix
  setting: staging_prefix
  status: create
  actions:
  - s3:GetObject
  - s3:PutObject
  - s3:DeleteObject
  details: TRN-2 writes, DLP-1 reads, DLP-2 deletes
- name: outgoing prefix
  kind: s3_prefix
  setting: outgoing_prefix
  status: create
  actions:
  - s3:GetObject
  - s3:PutObject
  details: DLP-1 writes, SEP-1 heads; never deleted or overwritten
- name: index prefix
  kind: s3_prefix
  setting: index_prefix
  status: create
  actions:
  - s3:GetObject
  - s3:PutObject
  details: DLP-1 writes, SEP-1 reads
- name: report prefix
  kind: s3_prefix
  setting: report_prefix
  status: create
  actions:
  - s3:PutObject
  details: the report framework task writes {run_id}.json
- name: package queue
  kind: sqs_queue
  setting: queue_url
  status: create
  actions:
  - sqs:ReceiveMessage
  - sqs:DeleteMessage
  - sqs:ChangeMessageVisibility
  - sqs:GetQueueAttributes
  details: visibility timeout 21600 s, retention 4 days, SSE-SQS, redrive to the DLQ maxReceiveCount 3. Policy allows s3.amazonaws.com
    sqs:SendMessage with aws:SourceArn = the bucket ARN and aws:SourceAccount = aws_account.
- name: package DLQ
  kind: sqs_dlq
  setting: dlq_url
  status: create
  actions:
  - sqs:GetQueueAttributes
  details: retention 14 days, SSE-SQS; alarm on ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible > 0
- name: bucket notification
  kind: s3_notification
  setting: source_bucket
  status: create
  actions:
  - s3:GetBucketNotification
  - s3:PutBucketNotification
  details: IaC only. Read the existing configuration (1 QueueConfiguration), add s3:ObjectCreated:* with prefix {incoming_prefix}
    and suffix .zip → queue_url, keep every existing rule. On overlap the owner decides (Q-TRG-1).
- name: bucket KMS key
  kind: kms_key
  setting: kms_key_arn
  status: existing
  actions:
  - kms:Decrypt
  - kms:GenerateDataKey
  details: bucket default SSE-KMS key (from the probe). No sse param is passed; objects inherit the default encryption.
- name: lifecycle rule
  kind: other
  setting: source_bucket
  status: create
  actions:
  - s3:GetLifecycleConfiguration
  - s3:PutLifecycleConfiguration
  details: IaC only (SUG-1). Expire noncurrent versions under incoming_prefix, processing_prefix and staging_prefix after
    30 days, and remove expired delete markers; merge with existing rules.
